title: Drainage Seton With Flap Versus EAS Preserving Seton in Treatment of Transsphincteric Anal Fistula
brief_summary: Patients with high trans-sphincteric anal fistula will be randomized to one of two equal group: group 1 will have drainage seton with mucosal advancement flap and group 2 will undergo external anal sphincter sparing seton
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients suffering from high trans-sphincteric anal fistula

Exclusion Criteria:

* Acute sepsis.
* Specific cause of fistula e.g. Crohn's disease
* Strictured anorectum.
* Any degree of incontinence
* Recurrent anal fistula.
* Low anal fistula.
* Previous anorectal surgery.
